query: Al Aseel Hotel, Najma, Doha, Qatar
name: Al Aseel Hotel
description: Chic quarters, some with Gulf views, in an upscale hotel offering dining, a spa & an outdoor pool.

reviews_data.review_text: The room carpet was dirty. no sandals for bathroom and when I ask reception say no stock.
The reception staff behaved very poorly; they only treat you well if they see you, and you are expected to offer a tip, which is not at all professional for a hotel like this.

After reading a number of good reviews I thought I would give the hotel a try, however it was a little disappointing and the hotel is quite old and the decor is dated.

Check in is slow and not streamlined with the need to be modernised.

The rooms are small and old and they have a safe, tea and coffee making facilities, a TV with a limited amount of English speaking channels and it is. Smart TV so you can watch Netflix or YouTube.

The beds are quite hard and not very comfortable and the pillows are also not very comfortable.

The bathroom is a reasonable size and the shower has a rainfall shower head and a hand held rose and the water pressure is weak.

There's not much within walkimg distance and the metro is about 600 metres away which isn't too convenient if you have luggage

Overall it was poor value for money and quite expensive for what you got. I wouldn't recommend this hotel for the price, there's much better hotels around and in better locations

The hotel is completely smoke-filled, very noisy at night and the beds are dirty. We booked a room for three (2 adults and a child) with the intention of getting 6 hours of sleep during an overnight layover in Doha. The smell of smoke in the lobby was so strong that we thought someone was smoking right there. The room was a little less, but still very strong - our clothes and hair completely smelled of cigarettes overnight. The third bed for the child was not ready immediately, and when it was brought to us, the employee did not bring bed linen, insistently convincing us that the child can sleep right on the mattress. After persistent demands, he brought a sheet, but never brought a duvet cover. The noise from the shouts from the street and unloading of cars did not let us sleep until 3 am.

I went on this hotel for check in again and  I accidentally stain the blanket. they ask me to pay 50qr for this small stain that both we knows it's will remove it quick.  I was shock bcz even on rooms even reciption they don't explain. That need to pay small mess.

The cashier in the bar (Mezzanine floor)  treats the customer very bad… he asked fhe every customer like you paid…? You paid? You paid? It may be his bad experience. But he has to check whether they are paying or not. He should not telling that so many people are not paying and getting out. Today everyone feel humiliated when he asked “you paid”. What i am thinking is this whole hotel administration is in the same way.

The room was terribly dirty. The carpet looks like it's a place of a crime scene, full of stains and burnt holes from cigarettes (in non-smoking room). Curtains were covered with stains. Walls were stained.
The bedding was dirty, staind and with hair, and when I asked to change it, the receptionist sent someone (who didn't introduce himself) and when he checked the bed, he said it's completely normal to have stains (and even human hair everywhere). I insisted that it should be changed, and only after that he sent someone to do it.
Room was missing some light bulbs as well. Cigarettes smell was everywhere in the corridors and in the room. There's no soundproof, you can clearly hear how neighbors are slamming doors.
When i was checking out next morning, receptionist held me for 10 mins, while they were checking that the room is clean and fine after me. That's ridiculous.
It's the worst experience ever and I will not advise anyone to stay there.

I stayed here for one night only, and while there were some positives, the overall experience was not great.

On the positive side, the room matched the pictures, and the staff were friendly. I was offered water at reception, allowed to check in late at 1am, and even check out late at 2pm, which I really appreciated.

Unfortunately, that’s where the good part mostly ends.

The Wi-Fi was extremely slow and unreliable, despite being told it was fast. The TV had very limited channels, and surprisingly Al Jazeera was missing. The carpet was very dirty, and clearly not well maintained.

The worst part was the outside noise. My window faced a Haraj market, and from 1am until morning there was constant noise from cars, people, and banging sounds. The sound insulation was almost zero. I couldn’t sleep properly at all.

The bed was quite stiff, and the towels in the bathroom smelled bad and looked very old and worn.

I don’t think I’ll be coming back. I hope the management takes this feedback seriously and fixes these issues for future guests.
